title: Nvidia’s Subtle Change to How It Counts Cash Flow Has Big Implications for Buybacks
source_used: KuCoin News flash carrying a Huo Xing Finance (MarsBit) report; the Wall Street Journal original was not available
key_facts: The WSJ headline says Nvidia has subtly changed how it counts cash flow, with big implications for buybacks.

A Huo Xing Finance report (via MarsBit and KuCoin) says that after expanding its repurchase authorization to $235 billion, Nvidia began stressing returning free cash flow after deducting 'strategic purposes' such as equity investments.

In the first half of its fiscal year (ended 26 July) Nvidia's net cash outflow from equity investments was $35.2 billion, plus $4.5 billion withheld for employee stock taxes and about $9 billion spent on buybacks.
Including those items, free cash flow would fall from the reported $69.9 billion to about $21.7 billion, down about 69%.
Nvidia added $24.9 billion in long-term debt over the same period.
Nvidia has not formally revised its traditional free cash flow formula, per the report.
Wall Street expects free cash flow above $330 billion for fiscal 2028.
quote_evidence: However, NVIDIA has not formally revised its traditional free cash flow calculation formula.
NVIDIA adjusted its free cash flow metric as part of its $235 billion share buyback program, now defining cash flow after deducting "strategic uses," including equity investments.
why_it_matters_hint: If equity investments are counted as strategic uses, much less cash is left for shareholders than the headline free cash flow suggests.
notes: WSJ returned HTTP 401. The relay is a crypto-news flash that does not name its own source and may derive from the WSJ piece; the 69% figure is the relay's own calculation. Treat as weakly sourced.
